actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset
inputs.name: seed

facts.text: LW-BenchHub describes itself as a unified benchmark hub built on Isaac Lab-Arena for embodied AI
The package description is 'Isaac Lab based Benchmark for Robotics'
The Gymnasium id Robocasa-Rl-G1LiftObjStateRL is registered with entry_point isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv and an env_cfg_entry_point in lw_benchhub_rl.lift_obj.lift_obj
LwEnvBuilder takes the arena environment, the parsed arguments and the RL config, and lets the RL config modify the environment config
LwTaskBase is the base class of the package's task definitions
LwTaskBase.modify_env_cfg sets an 8.0 s episode, a 1/100 s physics step (100 Hz) and decimation 2
The task termination config binds success to the task's check_success_caller
The LiftObj task is named LiftObj
The LiftObj task fixes the object pose at (2.94, -4.08, 0.95)
The LiftObj object is sampled from the cube group and marked graspable
LiftObj success requires the object root height to be at least 0.965 m
The G1 RL right-arm action is a joint-position action over right_shoulder.*, right_wrist.* and right_elbow.*
The Dex3 right hand uses a BinaryJointPositionActionCfg in the rl hand mode
The state-based G1 policy observation group concatenates joint position, joint velocity, the object pose command, the last action and the object position
The RL task resets the object with x and y offsets in (-0.08, 0.08) and a yaw in (0, 90) degrees

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds the task's object and robot randomization (LwTaskBase builds its rng from the context seed); this package's fake repeats a trajectory for a seed, but no upstream GPU run was made and bit-identical contact solving across machines is not claimed

gaps: Isaac Sim physics, PhysX contacts, the kitchen scene, the G1 USD articulation and the Dex3 hand are not modelled by this package's fake: it is a pure-Python analytic stand-in, not the upstream engine

the fake steps 20 ms of control time per tick (the environment period from an 8.0 s episode, a 1/100 s physics step and decimation 2 in LwTaskBase.modify_env_cfg); the underlying 10 ms physics substep is not integrated separately
the fake's action effects and reward are placeholder test data; only the task name, the fixed object height 0.95 m and the success threshold 0.965 m come from the clone

the real policy observation group dimension is computed at run time by the observation manager (ManagerBasedRLEnv._configure_gym_env_spaces); the fake publishes a reduced policy stand-in whose length is named in RESULT.json notes
no rendering, no cameras, no image observations and no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0
snapshot and restore are not offered by the upstream ManagerBasedRLEnv, so snapshot_restore is false
the upstream environment needs the Isaac Sim 5.0 and Isaac Lab GPU stack installed by install.sh; that path was not installed or run here

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
